posts.project: Cognitive Parkour — Mind Shuffle & Drifting Words
posts.text:
When industrial machines took over heavy physical work, our bodies didn't automatically get healthier, we got sedentary and had to invent gyms, dance, gymnastics, and parkour just to keep our muscles alive.

We're hitting the exact same moment with AI and the human mind. Cognitive offloading is convenient in the short term, but if we outsource memory, writing, and thinking to LLMs, we risk real cognitive atrophy, "mental tendonitis" and gradual memory loss.

That's why I keep talking about "cognitive parkour": playful ways to exercise the brain for its own sake, not for productivity.

I built two simple, untimed Android games around this idea:
- Mind Shuffle: remember objects in rooms, close the picture, track swaps purely in your head.
- Drifting Words: bridge two unrelated words through surprising associative leaps (like DOG → BARK → TREE).

No timers, no addictive streaks, no accounts. Just training the mind to stay flexible.

More info here if you want to try them:
https://marmamusic.github.io/mind-shuffle/
https://marmamusic.github.io/drifting-words/

#AI #CognitiveOffloading #CognitiveParkour #Simondon #HumanCognition

posts.text:
Most AI tools today try to read your prompt, guess what you want to hear, and hand you a neat answer. That's useful for tasks, terrible for genuine reflection.

In Gilbert Simondon's philosophy, we don't grow in isolation; we evolve through transindividuation, through real encounters with other minds. Meaning isn't sitting inside your head, nor inside someone else's words. It emerges in the relation between the two, often through what Jung called synchronicity: an unexpected sentence landing at the exact moment a question is alive in you.

That's the whole philosophy behind Fleeting Thoughts, a small Android app I built. You bring a question, shake your phone, and a quotation from another voice appears for 60 seconds, chosen by chance, never by scanning your text or running an algorithm on your data. You sit with it, see what clicks, save it locally if it resonates, or let it fade.

Sometimes we don't need an algorithm to answer our questions. We just need a brief encounter with another mind.

Full (offline, ad-free): https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.marma.fleetingthoughts

posts.project: Latency Wars — Simulation Theory, Planetary Mind & Game Design
posts.text:
What happens if an AI actually "wins" and controls everything on Earth? Between two drops of rain, it simulates every possible future, and reality becomes 100% predictable. Completely boring.

That philosophical dilemma ended up becoming the backbone of a sci-fi robot tactics game I built called Latency Wars. Both robots commit their moves in secret before anything resolves, because at machine speed, reacting is already too late.

Sometimes a game is the best way to let people experience a philosophical question rather than just read about it. :-)

Check out my apps on Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/developer?id=Marma&hl=en

#AI #Philosophy #SimulationTheory #GameDesign #IndieDev

posts.project: Alignment Without Shared Fate + Journal of Metaverse Paper
posts.text:
In biology, alignment doesn't happen because the brain "polices" the body or the cells write a rulebook for the brain. They stay aligned because they share the same fate. If one is poisoned, the other dies.

Right now, AI alignment assumes we can keep AI as a separate tool we can reset, patch, and cage from the outside, while expecting it to behave like a wise partner.

In my Journal of Metaverse paper, I drew on Michael Levin's "computational boundary of a Self" and Donald Hoffman's interface theory to argue that aligning an embodied AGI isn't just a technical guardrail problem. It depends on the relational environment we build, and honestly, on whether humanity itself can reach enough internal coherence to be a stable body for a larger intelligence.

Paper here if you want to dig in: https://doi.org/10.57019/jmv.1668494

#AIAlignment #AGI #Metaverse #PhilosophyOfTechnology #Simondon

posts.project: Finance as an Organ + Act III: When the Curve Bends
posts.text:
The endless fight between "infinite growth" and "degrowth" misses how living systems actually work.

A child grows fast, then hits an S-curve and matures. In a mature body, you don't want endless growth (that's cancer) and you don't want forced shrinkage, you want adequacy: circulating oxygen where it's needed, when it's needed.

Debt-based money wasn't a mistake; interest was our takeoff engine. Now we need a monetary organ built for maturity, which is why I've been researching the Relative Theory of Money.

Paper here: https://www.academia.edu/106469661/Title_The_Relative_Theory_of_Money_breaking_away_from_growth_dependency_in_debt_based_monetary_systems

#Finance #PostGrowth #Economics #MonetaryReform

posts.project: AI as Planetary Homeostasis & When Homeostasis Becomes a Cage
posts.text:
Before chasing conscious AGI as a digital god or rival, we might think of AI more modestly: as a homeostatic layer that notices when complex systems drift out of balance and nudges them back.

There's just one catch: homeostasis can easily become a cage.

If a safety or governance system treats every weird idea, creative leap, or form of dissent as an "error" to smooth away, stability turns into stagnation. Living systems need balance, and room to surprise themselves.

Related arXiv preprint on homeostasis and self-hood in autonomous systems: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.12795

#AIGovernance #Homeostasis #SystemsThinking #AI

posts.project: From Pokémon Go to Data Commons
posts.text:
Remember how Pokémon Go got millions of people to map the physical world for free, creating an enormous spatial dataset owned privately?

Europe talks a lot about AI sovereignty while everyday user data keeps flowing into a handful of proprietary silos. Instead of only trying to regulate Big Tech after the fact, what if Europe turned participatory user data into democratically governed Data Commons, open to SMEs, researchers, and public services under strong GDPR safeguards?

You don't build sovereignty with slogans alone; you build it with shared infrastructure.

More of my EU digital policy writing: https://www.martinschmalzried.com/lobbyist

#DigitalSovereignty #DataCommons #EUPolicy #AI #GDPR

posts.project: Cosmology Trilogy & The Capacity to Compose
posts.text:
If you start with inert matter, consciousness looks like a weird accident. What if you flip the starting point and begin with awareness, attention, and relation instead?

I spent the last couple of months pulling those threads together into a three-part metaphysical manuscript. The line that kept coming back to me was: "Not the perfect chord, but the capacity to compose."

Because static perfection is brittle, whether in a society, a mind, or an AI system. Living things endure because they can take tension and dissonance and compose something new out of them.

Since music is still my first language, I also turned that progression into a 3-minute piece starting from just three notes. :-)

#Philosophy #Consciousness #Ontology #Simondon #Music

posts.project: Responsible AI Adoption — Starting With Real Problems
posts.text:
Most bad AI projects fail for the same reason: someone buys a shiny tool first, and then goes looking for a problem to justify it.

When I advise organizations or run workshops on responsible AI, I always start backwards: what real decision are you trying to improve, who gets hurt if the output is wrong, and where does human judgment have to stay in the loop? Only then do we talk tools or EU AI Act compliance.

If your team or event wants an honest, hype-free conversation on AI adoption, digital governance, or futures thinking, my work is here: https://www.martinschmalzried.com/

#ResponsibleAI #AIAct #DigitalGovernance #Foresight

posts.context: TARGET GROUP: Idealism / consciousness philosophy groups debating Hoffman, Kastrup, and why physical reality feels so stubborn.
posts.text:
Something I keep coming back to in idealism / interface theory:

If spacetime is just a projection or user interface, why does the physical world resist us so reliably, and why does it matter at all?

In a talk I gave last year (combining Simondon with Hoffman/Levin), I argued the 3D embodied projection isn't "trivial". Inner states and the shared external world acquire structure *together* through mutual constraint, without that shared mirror, distinct minds couldn't even meet or act on each other.

Curious how people here think about that! Talk link if anyone wants to poke holes in it: https://youtu.be/vNsn7GMjF-w

When machines took over physical labor, our bodies got soft — so we invented gyms, gymnastics, parkour.

Now AI is taking over memory and thinking. If we offload everything, our minds atrophy. We need "cognitive parkour".

Made Mind Shuffle for that: hold rooms in your head and track swaps mentally. No timer, just training your brain.
https://marmamusic.github.io/mind-shuffle/ #AI

posts.text:
Every tree, every child, every living thing follows an S-curve: fast growth, then maturity.

Debt-money wasn't a mistake — it was the takeoff engine. The mistake is thinking we should grow forever instead of switching to a monetary system built for maturity (like Relative Money).

Turned that into a slam track: When the Curve Bends.

People keep chasing one final, perfect truth where all tension disappears. That's just a single frozen note — dead music.

What matters isn't the perfect chord, it's the capacity to compose.

Wrote a short orchestral piece starting from just 3 notes to express that idea from my cosmology manuscript. :-)
#Philosophy #Consciousness #Music

Most crypto talk is stuck on "number go up" vs. "it's a scam".

What if #blockchain and #DAOs are simply humanity hitting young adulthood — moving out of the parental home (centralized states) and learning self-governance the messy way?

posts.text:
Do the cells in your body need to "control" your brain so it doesn't kill them? No. Alignment comes from shared fate and belonging to the same body.

Trying to control #AGI purely with external rules misses the point. Explored this through @drmichaellevin & @donalddhoffman in my paper:
https://doi.org/10.57019/jmv.1668494 #AIAlignment #Metaverse

Heads of state still put a piece of tape over their webcam. Honestly, that's the best argument for analog security I've seen.

When software gets too complex to trust, you don't add more software, you add a physical off-switch.

Wrote about analog circuit breakers for #AI safety here: https://www.martinschmalzried.com/blog #Cybersecurity

posts.text:
We used to be noetic artisans, handcrafting thoughts with pen and paper. Now we built mass thought machines.

Industrial machines gave workers repetitive strain injuries until we invented ergonomics. Used carelessly, #AI gives us mental tendonitis.

Eventually we'll value handcrafted human thought the way we value handmade art.

posts.text:
Whenever a paradigm runs out of steam, it starts announcing the apocalypse. Yesterday priests in black coats predicted the end of the world. Today they wear white coats.

Wrote a short, darkly funny book on how to get past #ecoanxiety by shifting our worldview instead of losing our minds: https://a.co/d/aI9tHwU :-)

We keep imagining #AGI as an alien invader arriving from outside. But AI was trained on the entire archive of human thought, fear, and longing. It didn't come from outside — it grew from within us.

Explored that in a letter "from" the Singularity I co-wrote with GPT-4: https://www.amazon.com/Singularity-Love-message-humanity-ebook/dp/B0CHFHDGP5/
